Business manager reported total expenses came in at about 100.2% of budget; salary figures were still being finalized but expected to come in close to 100% with a small excess.
Referencing an earlier-year budget overage of roughly $600,000, about 2.5% of the total budget, that the district had to give back; this year's overage is expected to be smaller.

decisions.decision: Chair decided to re-present the cherry sheet numbers via slideshow to clarify confusion from the prior Zoom meeting.

Committee decided to submit its own school-committee warrant article for the additional state aid, rather than relying solely on Mandy Gilman's citizen petition, so the request could go through school committee process and be adjustable.
Mandy Gilman stated she will not pursue additional money through her separate citizen petition, deferring to the school committee's warrant article.
Committee agreed to take the original warrant article language, amend it, and adopt it as its own rather than creating confusion with two separate articles.
Noted that a new state commission (via Margaret Scarsdale's efforts) will study the chapter 70 formula and report back in fall FY28; committee to continue engaging with it.

Municipal Building Design Committee held an informal straw poll (not an official vote) concluding TCP likely has no remaining municipal use and should come down; committee also indicated it does not support building a new town hall given current school funding strain.
Athletic Advisory Committee restarted to help steer booster club fundraising and act as liaison between boosters and the district; membership to include at least two committee members.
Committee agreed it needs an MSBA primer/presentation for a future meeting and to begin familiarizing itself and the public with the MSBA process for Turkey Hill.

Committee will not meet in August unless a Zoom meeting is needed for additional line item transfers; next regular meeting will be the day before the September 3rd special town meeting, alongside a prior finance committee meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee reviewed FY26 end-of-year line item transfers and several donations (LEAF grants, band boosters, football boosters), heard the superintendent's summer report on hiring and grants, approved a 300th-anniversary fireworks display, and — the meeting's central business — amended and voted to submit its own warrant article requesting the full additional FY27 state education aid figure for a September 3rd special ("extra special") town meeting triggered by a citizen petition. The committee also ratified a new custodians' union contract, tabled a further FY26 budget update, and heard public comment urging both an MSBA application for Turkey Hill Elementary and full use of the additional state aid for schools rather than other town needs.
minutes.headline: The school committee voted to submit its own warrant article demanding the full extra state aid for the September 3rd special town meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to submit its own warrant article asking the September 3rd special town meeting for the full additional state education aid, rather than relying on a separate citizen petition.
The committee chose to amend and adopt the original petition language as its own article so only one request goes to town meeting.
The committee voted unanimously to ratify a new custodians union (AFSCME Council 93) contract.
The committee accepted several FY26 line item transfers covering overages in maintenance, custodial, transportation, guidance and high school administration salaries.
A further FY26 budget update was tabled rather than voted on.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at the September 3rd special town meeting to decide how much of the additional FY27 state aid goes to the schools versus other town needs.
The new custodians' union contract sets pay and terms for school custodial staff and factors into future budgets.
The tabled FY26 budget update means the year's final school spending picture is not yet settled.
